Update incorporating Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS):

- Dovish policy impulse: A 50 bp funds-rate cut (to 4.75–5.00%), lower IORB (4.9%) and ON RRP (4.8%), and “greater confidence” on disinflation remain supportive of easier financial conditions.
- SLOOS tempering factors: The latest SLOOS indicates banks continued to tighten standards and report weaker demand across key categories:
  - C&I: Net tightening for both large and small firms; weaker loan demand; wider spreads/stricter terms.
  - CRE: Broad tightening across property types with particularly weak demand; valuation and refinancing risks persist.
  - Consumer credit: Further tightening in credit cards, autos, and other consumer loans; higher minimum scores and required payments; delinquencies/charge-offs drifting up.
  - RRE/HELOC: Some categories show little change or only modest easing, but overall standards remain tighter-than-average; demand improvement likely gradual even with lower rates.
- Implication: The policy easing at the front end is partly offset by still-restrictive bank credit supply and soft loan demand, slowing transmission to Main Street (especially small business and CRE). This warrants a more cautious read than a purely dovish reaction.

Net: Still moderately positive for financial conditions and risk assets, but SLOOS tightness/weak demand further constrain the boost versus the FSR-only view.
